2607.25637.title: F(AI)2R: Who Did What, and Who Checked? Verifiable AI Provenance as an Executable Skill
2607.25637.paper_summary: F(AI)2R is FAIR research with AI in the loop, twice: an AI-assisted authoring pass and a machine-readable audit pass over every artefact. AI systems now draft, refactor, and verify research artefacts, yet their contributions are rarely recorded in a form a later human or machine can audit. Building on the original F(AI)2R experiment, we generalize its provenance model beyond scholarly writing into aiprov, a PROV-O extension covering any AI-in-the-loop artefact, and we package the method as an executable skill that an AI agent operates itself: setup asks the human operator for their ORCID ID, resolves their identity from the public registry, and scaffolds continuous integration that gates every push on graph conformance and publishes the current build of this very paper. The paper is its own case study. Every activity, claim, and source in its production is recorded in the repository's provenance graph under two invariants: no parentless claim, and verification rungs that only humans may grant.
2607.25637.paper_summary_zh: F(AI)2R 是將 AI 融入 FAIR 研究的兩個階段：一次是 AI 輔助的創作過程，另一次是對每個產物進行機器可讀的審核過程。AI 系統現在能夠起草、重構和驗證研究產物，但它們的貢獻很少以後來的人類或機器能夠審核的形式記錄下來。在原始的 F(AI)2R 實驗基礎上，我們將其來源模型推廣到學術寫作以外，進而發展出 aiprov，一個涵蓋任何 AI 在循環中的產物的 PROV-O 擴展，並將該方法包裝為一種可執行的技能，由 AI 代理自行操作：設置過程要求人類操作員提供其 ORCID ID，從公共登記處解析其身份，並搭建持續集成，對每次推送進行圖形一致性檢查，並發布這篇論文的當前版本。這篇論文本身就是一個案例研究。其生產過程中的每一個活動、主張和來源都在存儲庫的來源圖中記錄，遵循兩個不變條件：沒有無父主張，以及只有人類可以授予的驗證階梯。
2607.25637.author: Florian Krebs et.al.
